subject: Two data and two likelihood in  a Stan model: Is it possible?

messages.author: 53d479b609cc8ad3
messages.subject: Two data and two likelihood in  a Stan model: Is it possible?
parts:
Hi,
I have two data: One from the mothers (evolution of AB over time) and one from their offsprings (also evolution of AB over time).
We believe that the measurement of AB in mothers at delivery certainly affect the estimate of AB in infants over time.
And we want to put everything together, in one model.
So we want to have a non-linear mixed effect model for data of mothers, and use the prediction values from the last measurements of these mothers to be a covariate in the
non-linaer mixed effect model in infants.
It means we have two data, two likelihood and they are related to each other by the previous condition. We want to put all together.

Is it possible to do something like that in Stan?
I have read many threats in this Stan users mailing list but there seem to have no really good information for this question.
If yes, could you provide a link for a reference (if it is available) for at least give a general direction (if it is not a demanding request).

Thank you.

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Two data and two likelihood in a Stan model: Is it possible?
parts:
It's hard to say for certain given your description, but I strongly suspect that what you'd be looking for is a multivariate model with the measurement of the mother and measurement of the offspring as paired outcomes. If there are multiple offspring per mother, you'd still have a single "offspring mean" measurement paired with the mother measurement as multivariate outcome, then model the offspring as random deviates from this intercept.

Though possibly you're saying that you have data where you have many generations, with each offspring generation later becoming mothers, in which case I'd have to think further on how to do it.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Two data and two likelihood in a Stan model: Is it possible?
parts:
Hi Mike,

Thank you for your prompt response.

Please see the attachments the model for mothers and infants coded separately in Stan.
I actually have left-censoring observations in both data set and have longitudinal profile over time for both.
- In model in mothers: Assume a curve where the antibodies first increase, and after some time point h, it start falling with decade alpha_mum.
- In model in infants: Assume a curve where the antibodies first decrease with decay rate beta, after 2 months, it increase and then after h, decreases again.
In this model, antibodies of mothers at delivery (currently I am using the observed data, those values less than 5 are replaced by the predicted value obtained from the model of mothers) is considered as a covariate.
- In general, I want to combine the two data sets, and put the prediction of the antibodies of mothers at delivery as a covariate in the model of infants.

It is clear that it would involve in pairing the results, ID of mother and ID of infants.
I would like to have a sense whether we could combine the two data into one analysis like that.
Merci.
